page: Microsoft Azure M32ms_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance within the MSMediumMemoryv2 family, provisioned on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It runs on an x86_64 Intel processor architecture and supplies 32 dedicated vCPUs alongside 875.0 GB of system memory. This configuration establishes an extensive memory ratio of 27.34 GB per vCPU, explicitly targeting memory-bound enterprise systems.

The hardware configuration features zero local disk storage, necessitating the attachment of network-based block volumes such as Azure Premium Storage for operating system drives and persistent data. The instance does not include graphical processing units (GPUs) and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires network configuration through standard Azure virtual network routing mechanisms.

Resource allocation on the M32ms_v2 favors memory capacity significantly over computational compute density. The qualitative tradeoff involves relying on remote networked disks instead of fast local NVMe storage, which requires careful IOPS planning for write-heavy pipelines. The architecture is engineered primarily for memory-intensive workloads including massive in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning suites, large relational database management systems, and extensive caching tiers.

By prioritizing massive memory capacity over raw core density or local disk subsystems, the M32ms_v2 is designed for heavy in-memory enterprise operations.
